notes: The spec sheet is public but the original URL 404s. A corrected URL (with 'system' in the path) opens, but the extractor read only PDF metadata: Adobe Illustrator file created 2022-05-13, a 2022 launch asset. Its body text could not be read, so it shows no X compatibility or future-assay claims. Illumina's IVDR page (illumina.com/clinical/diagnostics/ivdr-guidance-resources.html) lists only three IVD sequencers, all IVDR Class A: MiSeqDx (≤15 Gb), NextSeq 550Dx (≤120 Gb) and NovaSeq 6000Dx (up to 6 Tb, 2x150). It does not mention a NovaSeq X Dx. The only X reference there is a navigation link to the X roadmap. Two web searches (standard mode) on NovaSeq X Dx, IVD mode and regulatory notices for 2025-26 found no X Dx product, kit or notice. The support-site results covered only the 6000Dx (IVDR Declaration of Conformity 200027832, covering S2/S4 kits; IVD-mode support docs). I did not try EUDAMED because it is a JavaScript app that is unlikely to be fetchable. Conclusion: no regulated X path is visible publicly as of 2026-10-12. This weakly fits the known evidence that the 6000 tail in regulated clinical work persists, but it adds nothing quantitative.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: As of Oct 2026 Illumina's public IVDR page lists no NovaSeq X IVD instrument; the only high-throughput IVD sequencer is the 6000Dx.
items.detail: The IVDR guidance page lists three IVD sequencers: MiSeqDx, NextSeq 550Dx and NovaSeq 6000Dx (up to 6 Tb, Class A). No X Dx appears, and the only X reference is a roadmap navigation banner. This is consistent with the known evidence that no FDA-approved test names the X. It also means labs running IVD-mode assays on the 6000Dx have no catalogued regulated X destination yet, so part of the clinical 6000 tail may be pinned until an X Dx is launched. The page is undated, so absence is weak evidence.

items.why_new: Known list covers the 6000Dx (2022) and TSO Comprehensive on the NextSeq 550Dx only; this checks the IVDR instrument list directly and finds no X Dx.
